proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.
\]
By \texttt{lem:causal-identification}, consistency and event-date transport imply the observed-law equality
\[
\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus (1) is proved from the causal target and is not used as its definition.

We first prove the upper bound. Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), one has \(\kappa=\lambda\), and the integer-order convention gives \(r=0\). Every nonfallback intercept is consequently a convex combination of the replicated means \(\overline Q_{st}\). Fix a design with \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\). By the corrected definition of \(g_{sT}\), the pair \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) belongs to every \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\). Hence \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\ne\varnothing\), so \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\) is impossible conditional on this design. Optimality of the selected certificate gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda+C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda+C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
&\qquad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda+C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda+C_V(Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The bandwidth floor gives
\[
(Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda.
\tag{3}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:holder-regression}, the support of \(K\), and (2)--(3) imply
\[
|\mathbb E(\widehat m_{s\ell}\mid z_0,(X_{st}),(Z_j))-m_s(z_{0s})|
\le C\{\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+(h_s^\star)^\lambda\}.
\tag{4}
\]
The terms in (4) are, respectively, selected-anchor extrapolation, the within-kernel Holder increment, and the increment from \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\) to \(z_{0s}\). Clipping cannot enlarge this error because the reference mean lies in \([-B,B]\).

Let \(m_\ell=|I_\ell|\). Balanced splitting gives \(m_\ell\ge N/3\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive and \(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\), while donor unbiasedness and conditional independence give
\[
\mathbb E\{\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^2\mid z_0\}
\le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{m_\ell}\le\frac{3SdC_\Sigma}{N}.
\]
Jensen's inequality therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E\{\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^{2\lambda}\mid z_0\}\le(3SdC_\Sigma/N)^\lambda.
\tag{5}
\]

Average the foldwise convex weights and denote the result by \(w_{st}\). Conditional on \(z_0,(X_{st})\), and the donors, define
\[
U_{si}=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)-\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}.
\]
Design-conditional centering gives \(\mathbb E(U_{si}\mid z_0,(X_{st}),(Z_j))=0\). Donor--panel separation and conditional cross-unit independence make the \(U_{si}\) independent across \((s,i)\). Since \(\sum_t w_{st}=1\), bounded wealth gives \(|U_{si}|\le4B\). Consequently
\[
\operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}\mathrel{\Big|}z_0,(X_{st}),(Z_j)\right)\le16B^2A.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (4)--(6), using fixed \(S\), and averaging over donors yields
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]
\le C\left[A+N^{-\lambda}+\left\{\sum_s\pi_s(h_s^\star)^\lambda\right\}^2\right]\le CR_D.
\tag{7}
\]

For the treated-mean converse, fix a bounded regression surface satisfying the disclosed modulus with slack, take \(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), and keep the design and donor laws fixed. Put \(b\in(0,B]\), and under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\) let independently
\[
\Pr_v\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\}=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
\qquad
\varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.
\]
For small fixed \(\gamma\), all probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\), consistency and both centering equalities hold, and the targets are separated by
\[
\Delta=4b\sum_s\pi_s\varepsilon_s=4\gamma\sqrt A.
\tag{8}
\]
Their Hellinger affinity is
\[
\prod_s(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}\ge\exp(-8\gamma^2/b^2),
\]
using \(\log(1-x)\ge-2x\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\). Cauchy--Schwarz bounds total variation strictly below one. Assigning any estimator to the nearer target and integrating the smaller density gives
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]\ge cA.
\tag{9}
\]
Under the displayed compatibility condition, \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} gives target separation at least \(c_0N^{-\lambda/2}\) and total variation bounded away from one. The same nearer-target test gives
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]\ge cN^{-\lambda}.
\tag{10}
\]
Taking the larger of (9) and (10) proves the lower bound. Equations (2)--(7) prove the upper bound without any temporal independence within a unit.

Averaging (7) and applying \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} gives
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0]
\le C\left[A+\left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\right]=CR_\star,
\tag{16}
\]
where \(D_T=\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\). Fixed \(S\) permits Cauchy--Schwarz to move the moment bound through the weighted sum, and the \(CT^{-2}\) fallback contribution is absorbed by \(D_T\).

For the converse, (9) gives \(cA\), \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} gives \(cN^{-\lambda}\), and \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} gives \(cD_T\). In each case, if two targets are separated by \(\Delta\) and total variation is at most \(1-\eta\), assigning an estimator to the nearer target gives maximal squared risk at least \(\Delta^2\eta/8\).

Put \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\). Direct algebra gives
\[
(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}=a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}\le a_s\vee b.
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed,
\[
\left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
\le2S\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}\le C(A+D_T).
\tag{17}
\]
Selecting the largest of the three lower-bound subexperiments proves the reverse inequality in (16).

On the independent-calendar subclass, the upper bound follows from the no-log part of the helper lemma. For the converse, take a ball of radius \(cT^{-1/d}\) about \(z_{01}\) and two Holder regressions that agree off that ball and differ at its center by \(cT^{-\lambda/d}\). The probability that \(T\) independent design points miss the ball satisfies
\[
(1-p_T)^T\ge c_0>0,\qquad p_T\le C_Xv_dc^d/T,
\]
for sufficiently small fixed \(c\). On this event the observed regression experiments coincide, so the common-submeasure testing argument gives squared risk at least \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\). Adding a common small affine or asymmetric-cusp component preserves the disclosed attainable modulus under the compatibility condition. This proves the independent-calendar result. Substituting \(S=1\), \(d=1\), and \(n_1=n\) gives the final display, while (17) proves the redundancy assertion.

On the regular branch and conditional on the design and donors, the centered unit-history contrasts in (6) are independent, have mean zero, and each uncentered contrast lies in \([-2B,2B]\). For \(a\le V\le b\), convexity of the exponential gives
\[
\mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}\le\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}.
\]
Multiplication over \((s,i)\) and exponential Markov therefore imply
\[
\Pr\left\{\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}\right|>r_{\mathrm{unit}}\mathrel{\Big|}z_0,(X_{st}),(Z_j)\right\}\le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2.
\tag{18}
\]
The linear term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) is the bounded-range correction, and it does not change the rate because \(M_w\le A_w^{1/2}\).

For the calendar radius, replace successive odd and even retained block vectors by independent copies. The definition of beta mixing bounds the total replacement error by \(2SK_T\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\). Conditional on the coupled design folds, each independent centered retained-block score has range at most \(L_k\). The exponential bound used for (18), separately on the two parities, therefore gives the first term in the defining constraint for \(x_{\mathrm{cal}}\). The discarded indices contribute at most \(L_{\mathcal G}\), and the treated means are covered by \(r_B\). Hence
\[
\Pr\{|\widehat\tau-\mathbb E\widehat\tau|>r_{\mathrm{cal}}\mid z_0\}\le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2.
\tag{19}
\]
The union bound shows that both (18) and (19) hold with probability at least \(1-\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}\); on that event the stochastic error is bounded by \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}\wedge r_{\mathrm{cal}}\). Thus no positive variance or asymptotic normal approximation is required.

For a donor fold of size at least \(N/3\), spectral clipping gives \(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I\), whence
\[
\mathbb E\left[N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\mid z_0\right]
\le\frac{2N}{c_\Sigma|I_\ell|}\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)
\le\frac{6SdC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.
\]
Markov's inequality and a union bound over at most two folds, with the displayed \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\), yield
\[
\Pr\left\{\max_\ell\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2>q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\mathrel{\Big|}z_0\right\}\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{20}
\]
Projection is nonexpansive, and \(\widehat\Sigma\preceq2C_\Sigma I\). On the complement of the event in (20), Holder continuity, the selected certificate, and the triangle inequality bound the conditional bias by \(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\). Combining (18)--(20) proves coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) on the regular branch. The full-range interval covers on every bad branch because bounded wealth and the causal target give \(\tau(z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\).

For expected length, \(r=0\) makes \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\), so
\[
r_{\mathrm{unit}}\le C_\alpha A^{1/2}.
\]
Since \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}\le r_{\mathrm{unit}}\), no calendar-block range term can enlarge expected length. Equations (2), (5), and \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} give
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\mid z_0)
\le C\left[A^{1/2}+\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}+\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}+N^{-\lambda/2}\right].
\tag{21}
\]
All deterministic small-sample bad branches disappear along the growth arrays. The remaining full-range contribution is at most
\[
4B\Pr(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0)\le CT^{-2},
\]
which is absorbed by the spacing term in (21). Equations (17) and (21) prove the expected-length upper bound. The independent-calendar assertion follows from the no-log part of the helper lemma.

For the converse, suppose two laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) possess a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\). Uniform coverage and the union bound within \(\nu\) give
\[
\max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.
\tag{22}
\]
Choose \(\gamma\) in (8) small enough that the sign experiment has common mass exceeding \(2\alpha\); (22) gives \(c_\alpha A^{1/2}\). In the explicit construction underlying \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family}, replace its center-displacement constant by a smaller positive constant. Its affinity tends to one with that constant, while target separation remains \(c_\alpha N^{-\lambda/2}\); (22) gives the donor lower bound. Finally, \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies common mass greater than \(2\alpha\) and target separation \(c_\alpha\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\). The independent-calendar empty-ball construction in the marginal proof supplies the no-log counterpart. Taking the largest channel and applying (17) proves the lower bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), the kernel is bounded and continuous and is bounded away from zero on a ball about the origin, and \(c_G\) satisfies the stated population-Gram compatibility bound. Under \texttt{ass:design-density} and \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}, for each fixed cohort and interior \(z_0\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}\mid z_0]
\le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}+N^{-\lambda}+\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right)^{2\lambda/d}\right\}.
\]
The same assertion with exponent \(\lambda\) holds after taking square roots. Moreover, \(\sup_P\Pr_P(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0)\le CT^{-2}\). On the independent-calendar subclass, the logarithmic spacing term is replaced by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Continuity and positivity of the fixed kernel on a smaller ball provide \(k_0>0\) and \(\eta\in(0,1)\) such that \(K(v)\ge k_0\) when \(\|v\|_2\le\eta\). For \(b\le\delta_0/\eta\), interiority and the density lower bound give
\[
p_b:=\Pr\{\|X_{st}-z_{0s}\|_2\le\eta b\mid z_0\}\ge c_Xv_d\eta^db^d=:c_pb^d,
\tag{11}
\]
where \(v_d\) is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball. Let \(M_b\) count these visits. Since \(r=0\),
\[
G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\ge\frac{k_0M_b}{Tb^d}.
\tag{12}
\]

Partition the calendar into consecutive blocks of length \(a_T\), and separate odd from even blocks. By the definition of the beta coefficient, replacing successive blocks in either parity by independent copies changes the joint law in total variation by at most the sum of the intervening coefficients. The total replacement error is therefore
\[
2K_T\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\le CT^{-2}.
\tag{13}
\]
For an independent collection of block counts \(Y_j\in[0,a_T]\), convexity gives
\[
\mathbb E(e^{-\theta Y_j})\le1-\frac{1-e^{-\theta a_T}}{a_T}\mathbb E(Y_j)
\le\exp\left\{-\frac{1-e^{-\theta a_T}}{a_T}\mathbb E(Y_j)\right\}.
\]
Exponential Markov's inequality with \(\theta=a_T^{-1}\), applied to both parities and combined with (13), yields constants \(c_1,C_1>0\) such that
\[
\Pr\{M_b\le c_1Tb^d\mid z_0\}\le C_1\exp\{-c_1Tb^d/a_T\}+C_1T^{-2}.
\tag{14}
\]
The corrected choice of \(c_G\) makes (12) coercive on the complement of the event in (14).

Let
\[
b_\circ=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\vee N^{-1/2}\vee\{a_T/T\}^{1/d}
\]
and let \(b_q\) be the first dyadic grid point not below \(2^qb_\circ\). Equations (12)--(14) imply
\[
\Pr\{h_s^\star>Cb_q\mid z_0\}\le C\exp(-c2^{qd})+CT^{-2}.
\tag{15}
\]
Summing the dyadic tail in (15) gives
\[
\mathbb E[(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}\mid z_0]\le Cb_\circ^{2\lambda}+CT^{-2}.
\]
Because \(a_T\asymp\log(T\vee2)\) and \(2\lambda/d\le2\), this proves the asserted moment bound. The event \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\) is contained in the failure event at the top of the grid, giving its \(CT^{-2}\) bound. The exponent-\(\lambda\) assertion follows by the same tail sum or by Cauchy--Schwarz. Under calendar independence no replacement is required and blocks of length one may be used, so \(a_T\) is replaced by \(1\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\). Under \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that, for every growth array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), every interior realized path \(z_0\), and every exact design array with \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for all \(s\),
\[
c\left(\left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}\vee N^{-\lambda}\right)
\le\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]\le CR_D.
\]
For the repaired anchor search, \(\Pr_P(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0,(X_{st}))=0\) on these design arrays. No two-sided conditional lower bound by the entire \(R_D\) is asserted: Gram coercivity alone does not make its realized-design term an optimal-recovery lower bound.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original two-sided conditional claim is false on the stated fixed-design class. A Gram lower bound makes the repaired local fit feasible but is not an optimal-recovery lower bound: an exact design can contain a point at the evaluation path, making the target estimable from its replicated mean, while the normalized Gram threshold is first crossed at a much larger bandwidth. For \(\lambda>1\), Gram coercivity also controls the squared local-polynomial weights but not their \(\ell_1\) norm; with unrestricted within-unit temporal dependence the conditional variance can exceed \(R_D\). The proposed claim preserves the proved positive conditional oracle upper bound and the treated and donor converses in the scalar-modulus regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), without assuming the missing sharpness property.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\). Under the regular random-design law, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus},
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0]\asymp R_\star.
\]
The geometric beta-mixing spacing term is \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\); on the independent-calendar subclass it is \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\). The oracle region is \(N^{-\lambda}=o(R_{\mathrm{or}})\), the generated-proxy region is \(R_{\mathrm{or}}=o(N^{-\lambda})\), and the boundary is \(N\asymp R_{\mathrm{or}}^{-1/\lambda}\). For fixed \(S\), the replicated-smoothing term is bounded by a fixed multiple of the maximum of the treated-mean and spacing terms and is not a separate nonredundant marginal phase. For \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), the independent-calendar rate is
\[
n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}\vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen final sentence omits the independent-calendar qualification and contradicts its own geometric-mixing definition of \(R_\star\). The proposed claim supplies the proved early-kill regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), retains the geometric beta-mixing logarithmic spacing penalty, states the iid no-log corollary explicitly, and removes the false claim that replicated smoothing is a fourth nonredundant marginal phase for fixed \(S\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\). Under \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, the total concentration interval \(C_\alpha\) in the corrected \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies
\[
\liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\Pr_P\{\tau(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid z_0\}\ge1-\alpha,
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0]\le CR_\star^{1/2}.
\]
Every data-measurable interval with the same uniform conditional coverage has worst-case conditional expected length at least \(cR_\star^{1/2}\). The interval uses bounded-range unit-history concentration, an explicit beta-mixing calendar-block coupling radius based on the selected weights, deterministic Holder and extrapolation bias, the full spectrally clipped donor covariance, and the full range on every declared bad branch; it never divides by a sample variance. Under independent calendars the spacing contribution is \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: A Wald radius based on a possibly zero block sample variance is not uniformly honest under bounded outcomes. The corrected total concentration interval is proved in the early-kill regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), where the selected local-constant weights have unit \(\ell_1\) norm and conditional cross-unit independence gives a valid bounded-history radius despite unrestricted within-unit temporal dependence.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For each cohort \(s\), let \(\mathcal B_s\) be the finite dyadic grid from \(b_{0s}\) to \(1\), and define
\[
g_{sT}(z_0)=\min\left\{b\in\mathcal B_s:\lambda_{\min}\{G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\}\ge c_G\right\}.
\]
If the displayed set is empty, set \(g_{sT}(z_0)=1\) and record that the set was empty. Thus a value \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) is an attained response-independent coercive bandwidth, rather than an infimum over a nonmonotone continuum or over an unobserved tube.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The old infimum ranged over a nonmonotone continuum and need not be attained at a dyadic bandwidth. The corrected radius is the attained dyadic pointwise coercive bandwidth actually used as the oracle comparison.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Set \(h_s^{\star}=g_{sT}(z_0)\). Because every element of \(\mathcal B_s\) is at least \(b_{0s}=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\vee N^{-1/2}\),
\[
(Tn_s(h_s^{\star})^d)^{-1/2}\le (h_s^{\star})^\lambda.
\]
Define
\[
R_D=\left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}\vee
\left[\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{(h_s^{\star})^\lambda+(Tn_s(h_s^{\star})^d)^{-1/2}\right\}\right]^2\vee N^{-\kappa}.
\]
proposed_definition_changes.reason: After correcting the realized geometry, the oracle bandwidth is its attained grid value; the bandwidth floor then proves the displayed variance-bias comparison.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Set \(K_N=\min\{2,N\}\), assign donors to the deterministic balanced folds \(I_\ell\), compute \(\overline Z_\ell\), and put \(\widetilde z_\ell=\Pi_{([0,1]^d)^S}(\overline Z_\ell)\). Form \(\overline Q_{st}=n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}Q_{sti}\). For each \((s,\ell)\), let
\[
\mathcal A_{s\ell}=\left\{(u,b)\in[0,1]^d\times\mathcal B_s:\lambda_{\min}\{G_{sT}(u,b)\}\ge c_G\right\}
\]
and minimize on this set the response-independent certificate
\[
\Gamma_{s\ell}(u,b)=C_H\|u-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\kappa+C_Hb^\lambda+C_V(Tn_sb^d)^{-1/2}.
\]
The selected pair \((\widehat u_{s\ell},\widehat h_{s\ell})\) is the lexicographically first exact minimizer, first in \(b\) and then in the coordinates of \(u\). Continuity of the fixed kernel makes \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\) compact and \(\Gamma_{s\ell}\) continuous, so this rule is well defined and Borel measurable. At the selected pair, use the intercept of the order-\(r\) tensor local-polynomial fit and clip it to \([-B,B]\); the intercept estimates \(m_s(\widetilde z_{\ell s})\), with \(C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\kappa\) charged as extrapolation bias. If \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\) is empty, record \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\) and use the clipped pooled mean, with recorded bandwidth \(1\). Average the fold values to obtain \(\widehat m_s\), and set
\[
\widehat\tau=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s\right\}.
\]
All searches, equality cases, projections, clipping operations, and fallbacks are deterministic and total.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The old rule could fail whenever a generated center left the fixed tube. The corrected response-independent optimization searches coercive anchors and charges Holder extrapolation to the generated center, while retaining clipping and a total fallback.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Put \(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha/2\). On the regular branch, let \(w_{st}\) be the actual response weight obtained by averaging the selected foldwise intercept weights. Define
\[
A_w=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right)^2,
\qquad
M_w=\max_{1\le s\le S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right),
\]
and
\[
r_{\mathrm{unit}}=B\{8A_w\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\}^{1/2}+\frac{8B}{3}M_w\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}).
\]
Using the complete retained blocks \(J_k\) separated by gaps of length \(a_T\), form cross-fitted block scores with the actual weights. Let \(\mathcal G_T\) be the set of discarded and incomplete-block indices, and put
\[
L_k=4B\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\sum_{t\in J_k}|w_{st}|,
\qquad
L_{\mathcal G}=2B\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\sum_{t\in\mathcal G_T}|w_{st}|.
\]
Define
\[
x_{\mathrm{cal}}=\inf\left\{x\ge0:
4\exp\left(-\frac{2x^2}{\sum_{k=1}^{K_T}L_k^2}\right)
+2SK_T\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2\right\},
\]
with the usual convention when all \(L_k=0\), and let
\[
r_B=B\left\{8\log(16/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}^{1/2}
+\frac{8B}{3}\log(16/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\max_s\frac{\pi_s}{n_s},
\qquad
r_{\mathrm{cal}}=r_B+L_{\mathcal G}+x_{\mathrm{cal}}.
\]
If the defining set for \(x_{\mathrm{cal}}\) is empty, declare the calendar branch unusable. This is an explicit scalar optimization and uses neither an estimated variance nor division. Since both concentration constructions are valid, put \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}\wedge r_{\mathrm{cal}}\). For \(N\ge2\), spectrally clip the full donor covariance estimator to \([c_\Sigma/2,2C_\Sigma]\), and set
\[
q_{\mathrm{don}}=\left\{\frac{32SdC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
Define
\[
r_{\mathrm{bias}}=C_H\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sK_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}\left(\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\kappa+\widehat h_{s\ell}^{\lambda}\right),
\qquad
r_{\mathrm{don}}=C_H(q_{\mathrm{don}}/\sqrt N)^\kappa,
\]
and
\[
R_\alpha=r_{\mathrm{samp}}+r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}},
\qquad
C_\alpha=[\widehat\tau-R_\alpha,\widehat\tau+R_\alpha]\cap[-2B,2B].
\]
If \(N<2\), some \(n_s<2\), fewer than two usable retained blocks exist, a cross-fit is empty, the calendar coupling budget is nonpositive, a candidate set \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\) is empty, or any numerical input is undefined or nonfinite, set \(C_\alpha=[-2B,2B]\). Hence no sample variance is divided by, and the bounded-range correction is explicit.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Uniform coverage requires bounded-range concentration and a donor ellipsoid with the covariance-comparison constants. The correction removes every division by an estimated variance and assigns the full range on all bad branches.

proposed_assumptions.condition: With \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\ 1\le v\le T})\), every cohort \(s\), unit \(i\), and deterministic \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_T)\in\mathbb R^T\) satisfy \[\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}v_t\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\mathrel{\Big|}z_0,\mathcal X\right)\le B^2\left(1+\frac{8\beta_0}{1-\rho_0}\right)\sum_{t=1}^{T}v_t^2.\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: This standard conditional covariance-operator bound is the missing premise needed to extend the higher-order local-polynomial conditional upper bound beyond \(\lambda=1\). Unconditional beta mixing of the joint design-response sequence does not imply it after conditioning on the entire realized design.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This bounds a separate response-noise covariance operator and does not assume any risk, rate, separation, or minimax conclusion.

proposed.def: A fixed continuous product kernel supported on the unit ball and bounded away from zero on a smaller ball about the origin.

proposed.name: Attained pointwise dyadic Gram radius
proposed.construction:
For each cohort \(s\), let \(\mathcal B_s\) be the finite dyadic grid from \(b_{0s}\) to \(1\), and define
\[
g_{sT}(z_0)=\min\left\{b\in\mathcal B_s:\lambda_{\min}\{G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\}\ge c_G\right\}.
\]
If the displayed set is empty, set \(g_{sT}(z_0)=1\) and record that the set was empty. Thus a value \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) is an attained response-independent coercive bandwidth, rather than an infimum over a nonmonotone continuum or over an unobserved tube.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The construction and its symbol closure must move together.

proposed.name: Conditional oracle upper-risk scale
proposed.construction:
Set \(h_s^{\star}=g_{sT}(z_0)\). Because every element of \(\mathcal B_s\) is at least \(b_{0s}=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\vee N^{-1/2}\),
\[
(Tn_s(h_s^{\star})^d)^{-1/2}\le (h_s^{\star})^\lambda.
\]
Define
\[
R_D=\left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}\vee
\left[\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{(h_s^{\star})^\lambda+(Tn_s(h_s^{\star})^d)^{-1/2}\right\}\right]^2\vee N^{-\kappa}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The rate is an attained oracle upper-risk scale after the conditional sharpness correction.

proposed.name: Replicated-donor anchor-extrapolation estimator
proposed.construction:
Set \(K_N=\min\{2,N\}\), assign donors to the deterministic balanced folds \(I_\ell\), compute \(\overline Z_\ell\), and put \(\widetilde z_\ell=\Pi_{([0,1]^d)^S}(\overline Z_\ell)\). Form \(\overline Q_{st}=n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}Q_{sti}\). For each \((s,\ell)\), let
\[
\mathcal A_{s\ell}=\left\{(u,b)\in[0,1]^d\times\mathcal B_s:\lambda_{\min}\{G_{sT}(u,b)\}\ge c_G\right\}
\]
and minimize on this set the response-independent certificate
\[
\Gamma_{s\ell}(u,b)=C_H\|u-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\kappa+C_Hb^\lambda+C_V(Tn_sb^d)^{-1/2}.
\]
The selected pair \((\widehat u_{s\ell},\widehat h_{s\ell})\) is the lexicographically first exact minimizer, first in \(b\) and then in the coordinates of \(u\). Continuity of the fixed kernel makes \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\) compact and \(\Gamma_{s\ell}\) continuous, so this rule is well defined and Borel measurable. At the selected pair, use the intercept of the order-\(r\) tensor local-polynomial fit and clip it to \([-B,B]\); the intercept estimates \(m_s(\widetilde z_{\ell s})\), with \(C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\kappa\) charged as extrapolation bias. If \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\) is empty, record \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\) and use the clipped pooled mean, with recorded bandwidth \(1\). Average the fold values to obtain \(\widehat m_s\), and set
\[
\widehat\tau=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s\right\}.
\]
All searches, equality cases, projections, clipping operations, and fallbacks are deterministic and total.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement updates both the construction and its free-symbol closure.

proposed.name: Total concentration calendar-block interval
proposed.construction:
Put \(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha/2\). On the regular branch, let \(w_{st}\) be the actual response weight obtained by averaging the selected foldwise intercept weights. Define
\[
A_w=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right)^2,
\qquad
M_w=\max_{1\le s\le S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right),
\]
and
\[
r_{\mathrm{unit}}=B\{8A_w\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\}^{1/2}+\frac{8B}{3}M_w\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}).
\]
Using the complete retained blocks \(J_k\) separated by gaps of length \(a_T\), form cross-fitted block scores with the actual weights. Let \(\mathcal G_T\) be the set of discarded and incomplete-block indices, and put
\[
L_k=4B\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\sum_{t\in J_k}|w_{st}|,
\qquad
L_{\mathcal G}=2B\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\sum_{t\in\mathcal G_T}|w_{st}|.
\]
Define
\[
x_{\mathrm{cal}}=\inf\left\{x\ge0:
4\exp\left(-\frac{2x^2}{\sum_{k=1}^{K_T}L_k^2}\right)
+2SK_T\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2\right\},
\]
with the usual convention when all \(L_k=0\), and let
\[
r_B=B\left\{8\log(16/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}^{1/2}
+\frac{8B}{3}\log(16/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\max_s\frac{\pi_s}{n_s},
\qquad
r_{\mathrm{cal}}=r_B+L_{\mathcal G}+x_{\mathrm{cal}}.
\]
If the defining set for \(x_{\mathrm{cal}}\) is empty, declare the calendar branch unusable. This is an explicit scalar optimization and uses neither an estimated variance nor division. Since both concentration constructions are valid, put \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}\wedge r_{\mathrm{cal}}\). For \(N\ge2\), spectrally clip the full donor covariance estimator to \([c_\Sigma/2,2C_\Sigma]\), and set
\[
q_{\mathrm{don}}=\left\{\frac{32SdC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
Define
\[
r_{\mathrm{bias}}=C_H\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sK_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}\left(\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\kappa+\widehat h_{s\ell}^{\lambda}\right),
\qquad
r_{\mathrm{don}}=C_H(q_{\mathrm{don}}/\sqrt N)^\kappa,
\]
and
\[
R_\alpha=r_{\mathrm{samp}}+r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}},
\qquad
C_\alpha=[\widehat\tau-R_\alpha,\widehat\tau+R_\alpha]\cap[-2B,2B].
\]
If \(N<2\), some \(n_s<2\), fewer than two usable retained blocks exist, a cross-fit is empty, the calendar coupling budget is nonpositive, a candidate set \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\) is empty, or any numerical input is undefined or nonfinite, set \(C_\alpha=[-2B,2B]\). Hence no sample variance is divided by, and the bounded-range correction is explicit.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement removes stale Wald symbols and records the total-concentration inputs.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\). Under \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that, for every growth array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), every interior realized path \(z_0\), and every exact design array with \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for all \(s\),
\[
c\left(\left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}\vee N^{-\lambda}\right)
\le\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]\le CR_D.
\]
For the repaired anchor search, \(\Pr_P(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0,(X_{st}))=0\) on these design arrays. No two-sided conditional lower bound by the entire \(R_D\) is asserted: Gram coercivity alone does not make its realized-design term an optimal-recovery lower bound.
proposed.justification: The repaired positive result is a conditional oracle upper bound with sharp treated-mean and generated-location converses in the early-kill regime.
proposed.gap: A Gram threshold alone is not a fixed-design optimal-recovery lower bound, and higher-order signed weights require conditional covariance stability.
proposed.consumer: The marginal theorem averages the oracle upper bound and supplies the sharp random-design result.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim, proof, and new dependencies must be installed atomically.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\). Under the regular random-design law, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus},
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0]\asymp R_\star.
\]
The geometric beta-mixing spacing term is \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\); on the independent-calendar subclass it is \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\). The oracle region is \(N^{-\lambda}=o(R_{\mathrm{or}})\), the generated-proxy region is \(R_{\mathrm{or}}=o(N^{-\lambda})\), and the boundary is \(N\asymp R_{\mathrm{or}}^{-1/\lambda}\). For fixed \(S\), the replicated-smoothing term is bounded by a fixed multiple of the maximum of the treated-mean and spacing terms and is not a separate nonredundant marginal phase. For \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), the independent-calendar rate is
\[
n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}\vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
proposed.justification: This is the sharp marginal early-kill frontier with the correct geometric-mixing spacing penalty and iid corollary.
proposed.gap: Higher-order smoothness needs a separate conditional signed-weight stability analysis.
proposed.consumer: Applications can locate the oracle/generated-proxy boundary and see that smoothing is redundant for fixed cohorts.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The iid qualification and phase redundancy change the formal statement and dependency spine.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\). Under \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, the total concentration interval \(C_\alpha\) in the corrected \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies
\[
\liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\Pr_P\{\tau(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid z_0\}\ge1-\alpha,
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0]\le CR_\star^{1/2}.
\]
Every data-measurable interval with the same uniform conditional coverage has worst-case conditional expected length at least \(cR_\star^{1/2}\). The interval uses bounded-range unit-history concentration, an explicit beta-mixing calendar-block coupling radius based on the selected weights, deterministic Holder and extrapolation bias, the full spectrally clipped donor covariance, and the full range on every declared bad branch; it never divides by a sample variance. Under independent calendars the spacing contribution is \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).
proposed.justification: The interval is uniformly honest by total concentration and attains the marginal frontier in the early-kill regime.
proposed.gap: Uniform higher-order inference awaits conditional covariance control for signed local-polynomial weights.
proposed.consumer: The interval is implementable without a positive variance denominator and exposes every bad-sample convention.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The concentration construction and narrowed proof require updated metadata.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\). Under event-date transport, design-conditional centering, the attainable-direction restriction, \(0<\lambda\le1\), and the displayed compatibility condition, the marginal minimax MSE is \(\asymp R_\star\) and the uniformly honest expected-length frontier is \(\asymp R_\star^{1/2}\); conditionally on the exact design, the repaired estimator has MSE at most \(CR_D\), but a matching lower bound for the realized-design term is not asserted.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The old metadata incorrectly advertised a conditional two-sided \(R_\star\) equality without the proved smoothness and compatibility scope.

prose_updates.tldr: The causal target is cohort-weighted buy-and-hold level wealth at a realized event path, identified by consistency and the explicitly untestable event-date transport equality. Historical paths are exact and only the event path is generated from donors. In the proved early-kill regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), a locality-respecting anchor estimator has conditional risk at most \(CR_D\), the marginal minimax MSE is \(R_\star\), and a total concentration interval has honest expected length \(R_\star^{1/2}\). Geometric beta mixing contributes the spacing term \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\); iid calendars remove the logarithm. For fixed finitely many cohorts, replicated smoothing is bounded by the treated-mean and spacing channels and is not a fourth nonredundant marginal phase. Exact constants and the higher-order conditional frontier remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical nonparametric regression fixes the evaluation point, generated-regressor expansions perturb every training coordinate, and errors-in-variables methods convolve latent training coordinates. None directly gives a realized-path causal frontier with exact historical paths, an external donor-generated query, replicated panel outcomes, and calendar dependence.
project_justification.niche: The panel architecture separates causal transport from observed-law centering and separates generated-location uncertainty from random-design spacing. Replication can make response noise smaller than the spatial resolution of the historical path cloud.
project_justification.fill: For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the repaired estimator searches coercive anchor-bandwidth pairs and charges extrapolation to each projected donor-fold center. Conditional cross-unit independence then controls the full unit-history contrast without requiring within-unit temporal independence. A geometric-mixing occupancy argument yields the sharp marginal logarithmic spacing term, while iid calendars give the no-log corollary. Total concentration, spectral clipping, deterministic bias radii, and full-range fallbacks yield uniformly honest expected length.

sampling_model.design: Each cohort has \(T\) exact historical paths with density bounded above and away from zero. Under geometric beta mixing, block occupancy gives spacing \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{1/d}\); independent calendars give \(T^{-1/d}\). The conditional oracle bound uses the attained dyadic Gram radius at the realized path.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks per window and \(n_s\) treated event levels. Conditional on the full exact design and \(z_0\), the prescribed conditional means hold and joint unit histories are independent across \((s,i)\); dependence between a unit's historical and event outcomes remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency links observed event wealth to treated potential wealth. Design-conditional centering controls observed sampling error, while event-date transport separately identifies the untreated event counterfactual; neither centering nor pseudo-event diagnostics proves transport.
sampling_model.overlap: Every realized cohort path is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary, and the design density is at least \(c_X\) locally.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated. Donor folds are projected to the path cube, and each fold uses a response-independent minimization over coercive anchors and dyadic bandwidths of extrapolation bias, smoothing bias, and a variance certificate. The honest interval uses actual selected weights, bounded-range concentration, a beta-mixing block coupling calculation, the full spectrally clipped donor covariance, and full-range bad-sample conventions.

prose_updates.related_work: Stone (1982), Fan (1993), and Fan et al. (1997) give the ordinary Holder and local-polynomial benchmark but not an external generated query with site replication. Gaiffas (2007) studies spatially normalized global sup-risk; here the logarithm instead follows from worst-case geometric beta-mixing occupancy, while the iid pointwise corollary has no logarithm. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) and Hahn and Ridder (2013) concern generated regressors entering training coordinates. Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) and Fan and Truong (1993) concern contaminated training coordinates and deconvolution. Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) is the closest clean-training random-center construction, but strong convexity makes its center error second order. Donoho (1994), Low (1997), and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) motivate modulus and bias-aware inference; Ferman (2021) and Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide relevant panel and full-covariance templates.
prose_updates.interpretation: The generated-proxy boundary is \(N\asymp R_{\mathrm{or}}^{-1/\lambda}\) in the proved regime. Above it, donor location is asymptotically negligible; below it, donor uncertainty determines both MSE and honest length. With fixed cohorts, the apparent replicated-smoothing term never dominates both treated-mean noise and spacing, so the marginal diagram has three nonredundant channels rather than four.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The two-sided conditional \(R_D\) frontier is not proved and is false under Gram coercivity alone: that condition certifies an estimator but does not certify a matching fixed-design optimal-recovery obstruction. For \(\lambda>1\), signed local-polynomial weights also require conditional covariance stability after conditioning on the full design; unconditional joint beta mixing does not supply it. The proved positive frontier is therefore restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\). Geometric beta mixing over triangular arrays has the logarithmic spacing penalty, while the iid-calendar corollary has spacing \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: Event-date transport remains an untestable causal restriction. The attainable-direction condition is also maintained and is used for the donor MSE and expected-length converses. The positive marginal and honest-length equivalences are proved for fixed \(S,d\), \(0<\lambda\le1\), and the displayed compatibility of \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\). Exact phase-intersection constants, higher-order smoothness, growing path dimension, adaptation, and uniform-in-path bands remain open.

statement_notes.justification: The repaired theorem gives a feasible conditional oracle upper bound and sharp treated and donor lower channels in the early-kill regime.
statement_notes.gap: The realized Gram radius is not itself a fixed-design optimal-recovery lower bound, so a two-sided conditional \(R_D\) equivalence is not claimed.
statement_notes.consumer: The marginal theorem averages the oracle bound and obtains sharpness from random-design occupancy.

statement_notes.justification: The marginal frontier is sharp for \(0<\lambda\le1\), with logarithmic spacing under geometric beta mixing and no logarithm under iid calendars.
statement_notes.gap: Higher-order signed-weight analysis remains outside the proved scope.
statement_notes.consumer: Applications can compare donor location, treated replication, and calendar spacing; replicated smoothing is redundant for fixed cohorts.

statement_notes.justification: A total concentration interval attains the square-root marginal rate without studentization.
statement_notes.gap: The honest higher-order extension needs conditional covariance control for signed weights.
statement_notes.consumer: Inference remains defined on zero-variance, empty-search, and small-sample realizations through explicit full-range conventions.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem is obsolete and false over the repaired class.  The class now imposes \(\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]\) almost surely through \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, so it does exclude the unrestricted event-outcome dependence on the realized training design used by its only witness.  The latest directive requires the exact-constant question to be restored as unresolved rather than answered negatively by this theorem.

The lemma's claimed laws do not belong to the displayed repaired model class.  In its nontrivial law, with \(E=\{X_1\le q\}\in\mathcal X\) and \(B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=b_*\mathbf 1_E\), one has \(\mathbb E[B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=b_*\mathbf 1_E\) but \(\mathbb E[B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]=b_*q\).  Because \(0<q<1\) and \(b_*>0\), these quantities differ with positive probability, violating \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  After deletion of the theorem that consumed it, no live inbound edge remains; the witness may be described only for the larger class obtained by deleting that assumption, as directed.
